name: Bo-Rukul
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. [2010 printout]. Fyem wordlist: the Fyem language of Central Nigeria and its affinities. Draft. 32 pp. [sister language fyam1238, read for context]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; Sec. 3.3 Tones cites Nettle (1998): two tones, no glides; no stress/accent statement.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. [2010 printout]. The Horom language of Central Nigeria and its affinities (Horom wordlist). Draft. 25 pp. [sister language horo1245, read for context]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; Sec. 3.3 Tones: two tones, mostly low; no stress/accent statement.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2006 [this printout 29 Aug 2010]. The Rukul language of Central Nigeria and its affinities. Draft circulated for comment. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. 25 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 3 Phonology (pp. 2-3) covers vowels, consonants and tones only: 'The tone system of Rukul is quite restricted, with only two tones. The majority of words appear all low tone.' Tones mostly unmarked in the wordlist; the words stress/accent do not occur in the document.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 1999. Field trip to record the status of some little-known Nigerian languages [Reports from Plateau field trips 1998-1999]. Ogmios 11. 3 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; sociolinguistic notes on Rukul and Bo (location, nomenclature, speaker numbers).

sources.citation: Nettle, Daniel. 1998. Materials from the South-Eastern Plateau languages of Nigeria (Fyem, Hórom and Mabo-Barukul). Afrika und Übersee 81: 253-279.

sources.note: The only other primary publication with Bo-Rukul (Mabo dialect) data; tagged phonology/tonology in Glottolog; may contain a remark on stress vs. tone that Blench's wordlist lacks.

sources.citation: Nettle, Daniel. 1998. The Fyem language of Northern Nigeria (Languages of the World/Materials 136). München: LINCOM Europa.

sources.note: Fullest phonological description of any Southeast Plateau language (Fyem, sister of Bo-Rukul); would show whether this subgroup is described with any stress/accent alongside tone, and Blench's Rukul phonology defers to it.
